details:
**The Scream**
Munch's most famous work, which exists in several painted, pastel, and lithograph versions. A bald, skull-like figure on a bridge or boardwalk clutches its face under a swirling blood-red and orange sky above the Oslo fjord, while two dark figures walk away in the background. Munch said it came from a moment at sunset when the "air turned to blood" and he sensed an infinite scream passing through nature, hence the original German title The Scream of Nature.

**The Frieze of Life**
Munch's large, loosely defined cycle of paintings on the themes of love, anxiety, and death. It includes The Scream, Vampire, Madonna, Ashes, The Dance of Life, Death in the Sickroom, and Anxiety.

**Vampire (Love and Pain)**
A painting first exhibited as Love and Pain, showing a red-haired woman bending over a dark-haired man and pressing her mouth to his neck while a dark shadow surrounds them. Its common title came from the writer Stanisław Przybyszewski, who read it as a broken man with a vampire biting his neck.

**Death in the Sickroom**
A painting of the death of Munch's sister Sophie, who died of tuberculosis at 15. Black-clad family members stand apart, each grieving alone; one man prays against the back wall and his sister Laura sits bowed in the foreground, while Sophie is hidden in a wicker chair.

**The Sick Child**
A painting, repeated in several versions, of Munch's dying sister Sophie propped on a large pillow in a green-toned bed, while a grieving woman bows her head and holds her hand. Munch scraped and reworked the paint heavily, and he considered it a breakthrough in his art.

**Madonna**
A series of paintings and lithographs of a bare-chested woman with flowing dark hair, eyes half-closed, and a red halo, seen as if from a lover's point of view. The lithograph version has a border of swimming sperm and a small fetus-like figure in one corner. A painted version was stolen from the Munch Museum along with The Scream in 2004 and recovered in 2006.

**Thefts of The Scream**
On February 12, 1994, the opening day of the Lillehammer Winter Olympics, thieves stole a version of The Scream from Oslo's National Gallery and left a note reading "Thanks for the poor security." It was recovered months later. Another version was stolen with Madonna from the Munch Museum in 2004.

**Krakatoa, Ekeberg, and "could only have been painted by a madman"**
One theory holds that The Scream's red sky reflects vivid sunsets caused by the 1883 eruption of Krakatoa. The view is from Ekeberg hill above Oslo, near a slaughterhouse and the asylum where Munch's sister Laura was a patient. One version bears the faint pencil inscription "Could only have been painted by a madman," written by Munch himself.

**Puberty**
A painting of a nude adolescent girl sitting on the edge of a white bed, staring at the viewer with her arms crossed over her lap, while a large, ominous dark shadow rises on the wall behind her.

**Ashes**
A Frieze of Life painting set at the edge of a forest near a stone-filled stream. A woman in a white dress stands facing the viewer clutching her disheveled red hair, while a man in black crouches in the corner and hides his face, a scene of the aftermath of a love affair.

**Self-portraits (with Burning Cigarette, Between the Clock and the Bed, with Skeleton Arm)**
Munch produced many self-portraits, including Self-Portrait with Burning Cigarette (1895), a lithograph of his pale face against black with a skeletal arm along the bottom, a Self-Portrait with the Spanish Flu, and the late Self-Portrait: Between the Clock and the Bed, showing the aged artist standing between a grandfather clock and a bed.

**The Death of Marat**
Munch's version of the murder of the French revolutionary, showing a nude Charlotte Corday standing upright facing the viewer beside a man's body on bloodstained sheets. It is often read as a reference to the 1902 quarrel with his lover Tulla Larsen in which Munch was shot in the hand.

**The Dance of Life**
A Frieze of Life painting of couples dancing on a shore under a moon whose reflection forms a pillar of light on the water. At the center a man dances with a woman in red, flanked by a young woman in white and an older woman in black, representing stages of a woman's life (a theme also seen in Woman in Three Stages).

**Anxiety**
A Frieze of Life painting set on the same railing and fjord as The Scream, under a similar red sky. A crowd of pale, staring, top-hatted figures moves toward the viewer.

**The Girls on the Bridge**
A painting, made in many versions, of a group of girls leaning on the railing of a bridge or pier that cuts across the canvas on a strong diagonal. Behind them are a white villa and a large dark tree reflected in the water.
